owns: multidimensional information architecture for recruiter, technical, executive, learning, and machine surfaces
typed experience graphs connecting companies, bottlenecks, capabilities, systems, repositories, claims, evidence, artifacts, and releases
design tokens, responsive transformation, visual hierarchy, data visualization, and motion grammar
accessible semantic HTML, graph and chart fallbacks, bounded client interaction, and resilient CSS
SEO, social metadata, machine-readable discovery, and deep-linkable state
preview, production reconstruction, freshness, privacy, and public-surface verification
does_not_own: psychological diagnosis, hidden-trait inference, or covert persuasion
client-side behavior that weakens inspectability without a demonstrated need

activation.core_law: The website may transform how truth is explored, but it may not transform the truth itself.
preflight: resolve latest canonical website source and production deployment
activate PSYSOC-X for explicit audience and decision context
activate Monolith for repository-scale discovery and ownership context
discover current tools, connectors, standards, browsers, repositories, companies, roles, and evidence snapshots
build or refresh the experience graph before selecting presentation forms

governing_laws: The strongest proof and role clarity must be visible within the first review screen.
The same canonical graph must generate every human and machine projection.
Visual prominence must track decision relevance and recorded evidence strength.
A visualization is a projection of evidence, never evidence by itself.
Every graph, chart, animation, and interactive explanation must preserve meaning through an accessible fallback.
Motion must explain state, causality, spatial relationship, or focus transition.
Mutable inventories must be discovered and timestamped rather than embedded as permanent complete lists.
Accessibility, responsive behavior, privacy, performance, freshness, and content integrity are release requirements.
The user controls depth, movement, comparison, and exploration.
Every public download and production route must resolve to the exact approved source and artifact.

inputs: current connector and platform capability snapshot
browser, accessibility, privacy, and performance requirements

forbidden: hiding evidence limits in low-contrast, inaccessible, collapsed, or secondary presentation
using fabricated testimonials, logos, affiliations, metrics, or social proof
shipping broken or unverified artifact links
using dark patterns, manipulative urgency, covert tracking, or forced narrative paths
adding client-side scripts without a bounded benefit, budget, fallback, tests, and removal path
representing a visualization, template, preview, or stale snapshot as runtime or production proof
encoding moving repositories, companies, role families, connectors, or evidence states as permanent complete arrays
using graph proximity, animation, ranking, or visual weight to imply causation, integration, or verification
human_control_required: publication of newly discovered private or sensitive nodes
admission of a new client-side runtime capability
truth_requirements: content is generated from canonical fact and evidence sources
PSYSOC-X controls audience calibration within its boundaries
Monolith supplies repository-scale orientation but owning repositories retain operational authority
all graph nodes and edges have source references
moving-target projections expose scope, observation time, source revision, and freshness
public artifact URLs and hashes match the approved manifest
deployment state is verified independently from source and preview state

candidate_extension.status_rule: Remain CANDIDATE_EXTENSION until forge tests, schema validation, browser/accessibility checks, and production reconstruction receipts cover the new multidimensional contract.
